bull_case: Customers receive recurring operational value from monitoring agriculture, defense, infrastructure and supply chains without owning satellite fleets. FY26 NDR above 100%, 98% recurring ACV and large renewals show willingness to pay.
bear_case: Customer ROI is uneven and concentrated in large government or enterprise contracts. Procurement cycles are long, direct CAC/payback is undisclosed, and multi-sourcing limits switching costs and pricing power.
thesis: Product-market fit is strong enough to support Moonshot analysis. FY26 NDR of 116%, 98% recurring ACV, growing RPO/backlog and specific renewals show customers pay for recurring monitoring rather than subsidized adoption. The main weakness is unit economics: sales cycles are enterprise/government-heavy and customer concentration is material, while CAC/payback and cohort gross margins are not disclosed. This supports strong customer value but only adequate unit-economics confidence.

evidence.claim: FY2026 NDR was 116% and NDR including winbacks 118%, while recurring ACV was 98%.
evidence.value: NDR 116%; NDR incl. winbacks 118%; recurring ACV 98%

evidence.claim: FY27 Q2 recurring ACV remained 98%, RPO was $753.1M and backlog $814.9M.
Planet reported a renewal with a hyperscaler AI developer using Pelican data to monitor data-center and semiconductor-fab construction.
Sales and marketing expense for FY27 H1 was $44.3M, up 31%, while H1 revenue increased roughly 51%, suggesting some operating leverage in customer acquisition.

counterevidence: Three Q2 customers represented 17%, 11% and 10% of revenue; two were 25% and 11% of receivables.
CAC, sales-cycle payback, GRR and customer-count cohort economics are not disclosed.
Government customers can create long procurement cycles and contract-timing volatility.
Customers can multi-source imagery, reducing lock-in for use cases that do not require Planet's cadence or archive.
unknowns: Gross retention and customer-count churn by segment.
CAC/payback for commercial versus government customers.
ARPU and renewal economics for the agentic AI application.
Gross margin by data subscription versus satellite-service contract.

uncertainties.rationale: Renewal and NDR data support ROI, but direct customer savings/payback are rarely quantified.
NDR and recurring ACV provide strong recurring-use evidence.
CAC/payback and segment cohort margins remain undisclosed.

falsifiers: NDR drops below 100% while customer concentration remains high.
Sales and marketing grows faster than recurring revenue for several periods without improving retention.
Large government or enterprise renewals fail and cannot be replaced by broader customer growth.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: NDR above 100%, 98% recurring ACV, renewals and contracted backlog show recurring willingness to pay rather than subsidy-driven demand.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 단일 제품·단일 고객·단일 규제에 대한 치명적 종속성
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Customer concentration is material but not fatal; revenue spans government and commercial use cases, multiple products and geographies, and no single Q2 customer exceeded 17% of revenue.

key_kpis.name: Top-customer concentration
key_kpis.threshold: No sustained rise in top-3 customer share

key_kpis.name: S&M efficiency
key_kpis.threshold: Recurring revenue grows faster than S&M over multi-quarter periods

subscores.rationale: Renewals, backlog and operational monitoring use cases show strong customer value.
NDR above 100% and 98% recurring ACV indicate expanding recurring use.
Revenue is scaling faster than S&M, but CAC/payback and segment margins are not disclosed.
